newsitem.title: UK: Argentine supermarket Disco gets downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine supermarket Disco gets downgrade.

text.p: Latin American brokerage BBV LatInvest on Monday downgraded Argentine supermarket chain Disco, citing the chance of delays in its expansion plans from a proposed new law regulating large supermarkets.
"We downgrade Disco to a "reduce" from a "buy" and would look at buying the stock back at the $8 level ($24 per ADR)," BBV LatInvest said in a statement released in London.
The stock closed on Friday at $8.90 on the Buenos Aires exchange.

"A new law being proposed to regulate the establishment of large supermarkets could delay the opening of Disco's new stores in Buenos Aires," it said, adding Disco planned to open nine new stores under a programme that forms the centrepiece of its growth strategy.
Disco is now trading on 19 times earnings, a 25 percent premimum to the Argentine market, the statement said.
"With possible delays caused by this new bill, the multiple could clearly rise further."

Last week Deutsche Morgan Grenfell downgraded Disco to "hold" from "buy" due to its recent strong market performance, while Caspian Securities downgraded it to "sell" from "market performer" citing an unattractive valuation. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
